templates.title: Contradiction seeker
templates.summary: A critic hunts one counterexample to a stated claim on a fixed budget; finding none is a pass, finding one sends it back to the builder.
templates.whenToUse: A claim can be broken by one concrete counterexample (a property, an invariant, an edge case), and a bounded search for it is worth more than an open-ended review.

templates.title: Debate then build
templates.summary: Two planners argue opposite approaches for a capped number of rounds, a judge writes the plan, a human approves it, and a small grind loop builds it.
templates.whenToUse: Short adversarial planning, then a small build graph: the right approach is genuinely unclear and a wrong choice is expensive to undo.

templates.title: Dual bar
templates.summary: A builder and an isolated critic loop against two lines: a reachable ship line that stops the loop, and an aspiration that only steers the findings.
templates.whenToUse: The work needs both a ship line and a directional aspiration: good enough to ship is clear, and better is worth pointing at without ever blocking.

templates.title: Fresh grind, rare judge
templates.summary: A fast builder grinds each phase against the tests; an expensive judge runs only at phase boundaries, against a phase checklist.
templates.whenToUse: Cheap iteration most steps, an expensive critic at phase boundaries: long work splits into phases that tests can drive but only judgment can sign off.

templates.title: Gauntlet, decomposed
templates.summary: A planner cuts the work into pieces and a human approves the cut; one piece at a time an owner polishes while a fresh frontier critic compares captures blind against the reference; an integrator and a final blind comparison close it.
templates.whenToUse: A rendered artifact must match a named reference and is too large for one owner and one critic: the pieces have real seams, each can be captured and judged alone, and they are coupled enough to build in sequence.

credits.name: Matt Shumer's Gauntlet Loop and the Claude of Duty repository
credits.note: decompose, then builder plus fresh critic per piece against a real reference, blind side by side; here bounded, and pieces run in sequence because the repository's own note says fan-out lost on coupled work

templates.title: Grind loop
templates.summary: A fast builder works against the test suite until it passes, bounded by rounds and minutes.
templates.whenToUse: Done and good are the same: tests, types or a task list supply the back pressure, so a passing check is the finish line.

templates.title: Heterogeneous critic
templates.summary: The review gate with the critic on a different model tier from the builder, so it does not share the builder's blind spots.
templates.whenToUse: The judge should not share the builder's model when isolating taste or blind spots matters: a same-model critic keeps approving the mistakes the builder makes.

templates.title: Human-gated irreversible step
templates.summary: A human gate, then the one node that performs an irreversible action, then a stop: insert it before any merge, publish, spend or delete.
templates.whenToUse: A step cannot be undone (merge, spend, publish, delete) and must wait for a human decision; this fragment satisfies E_IRREVERSIBLE_NO_GATE.

templates.title: Merge queue
templates.summary: An integration check on the queued batch; a failure goes to a bisector that finds the change at fault and leaves the rest queued; a pass waits for a human, who lets one node land the batch.
templates.whenToUse: Several reviewed changes wait to land together and the integration command (build, lint, tests) is the arbiter: insert this before the host's stop node so a batch lands only green and only on a human's word.

credits.name: Steve Yegge's Gas Town Refinery
credits.note: a merge queue that integrates a batch, bisects on failure and lands by a human's word

templates.title: Metric sandwich
templates.summary: Cheap deterministic checks run first; an expensive critic judges only what they cannot see, and either failure returns to the builder.
templates.whenToUse: Cheap deterministic checks first, expensive judgment only on what those cannot see: lint and tests catch most failures, and a reviewer should not spend a round on them.

templates.title: Ownership, not swarm
templates.summary: Coupled subsystems get one owner each, in sequence; only the independent pieces fan out to fast workers; an integrator joins them and the tests close it.
templates.whenToUse: Coupled subsystems get one owner; fan out only the independent pieces. The work spans a shared core and several leaf pieces that touch nothing else.

credits.name: Claude of Duty process note (Matt Shumer)
credits.note: sequential ownership beat parallel fan-out on coupled systems in the repository's own write-up

templates.title: Patrol pulse
templates.summary: A scan lists candidate signals, a read-only investigator judges them against the project and the existing tickets, a writer files the new ones to the ticket store, and a human prioritises; one pulse is one run.
templates.whenToUse: Something should be looked at on a schedule (a log, a queue, a report) and the output of each look is a triaged record for a human, never a change: run the package under the harness's scheduler and each pulse is a run.

credits.name: u/croovies's "Lloyd" heartbeat orchestrator, as written up by explainx.ai (2026-08-14; a secondary source)
credits.note: a standing checklist per pulse, a read-only investigator, findings to a durable ticket store, humans prioritise

credits.name: Steve Yegge's Gas Town patrols
credits.note: patrol agents that loop by design; here one pulse is one run

templates.title: Ralph loop
templates.summary: A fresh builder takes the top unchecked item of a plan file each round, commits on green and appends what it learned to an agent file, until the plan is empty.
templates.whenToUse: The work is already a prioritised list of small items that tests can check one at a time, and you want a fresh context per item with the plan and an agent file as the only memory.

credits.name: Geoffrey Huntley's ralph loop
credits.note: one prompt piped into a fresh session per pass; one item of work per pass from a plan file; state on disk; the human as the brake, here replaced by stops

templates.title: Red-team loop
templates.summary: A separate attacker records reproducible failing traces; the builder sees only the traces, until no new one appears.
templates.whenToUse: A separate attacker should produce failing traces and the builder should see only those: hardening against inputs or abuse nobody has listed yet.

templates.title: Retrospective rewrite
templates.summary: A grind loop that ends, pass or fail, with a researcher reading the run's notes and proposing graph changes for the human to adopt.
templates.whenToUse: After a run, propose graph edits rather than rewriting mid-flight: the graph is being tuned across runs and the human wants every change as a proposal.

templates.title: Review gate
templates.summary: A builder works, an isolated critic checks the change against a written checklist, failures loop back, and a human approves the merge.
templates.whenToUse: Work, then a separate reviewer, then iterate or pass: the change needs a second pair of eyes against a checklist that already exists.

templates.title: Spec then loop
templates.summary: A planner writes the answer key, a human approves it, then a builder and an isolated critic loop against it.
templates.whenToUse: No external reference product exists: a planning pass writes an answer key (ACCEPTANCE.md) that becomes the bar. The default for zero-to-one work.

credits.name: Answer-key-first Gauntlet, a community modification of Matt Pocock's Wayfinder
credits.note: write the spec and a pass/fail answer key before the loop; the modification is known from a secondary write-up, not a primary source

templates.title: Specialist critic bank
templates.summary: Four fresh specialist critics review in parallel, a triage judge merges their findings by severity, and the change loops until nothing blocker or major remains.
templates.whenToUse: Multiple disjoint judges (correctness, security, performance, taste) should each look at the change, and their findings need merging by severity.

templates.title: Taste polish
templates.summary: One owner polishes an existing artifact while an isolated frontier critic compares readable captures against a named reference, bounded by rounds, budget and a human check-in.
templates.whenToUse: Done and good have split: the artifact works but must match a named, inspectable reference, and the polish can be judged from captures.

credits.name: Matt Shumer's Gauntlet Loop (Claude of Duty)
credits.note: the bounded form of the Gauntlet: one owner, an isolated critic against a named reference, real stops

templates.title: Tournament then judge
templates.summary: Three fast candidates build in parallel, a cheap check drops the broken ones, a frontier judge picks one finalist, and a builder finishes it.
templates.whenToUse: Cheap candidates, then spend the expensive critic on finalists: the approach is open, drafts are cheap, and comparing working options beats arguing about them.
